title: Go SDK — typed response mappers, streaming transformers, and retry semantics
creator: Lina Chen
description: Goal: Ship a small, ergonomic library inside the Go SDK that provides: (1) typed struct mappers for common Redwood response shapes, (2) composable streaming transformers that let callers apply decoding, filtering, and backoff/retry behavior without duplicating boilerplate, and (3) clear examples showing best practices for structured-output decoding and streaming-safe retries. Rationale: teams repeatedly reimplement similar decoding and streaming glue code. A lightweight canonical approach will improve correctness, reduce bugs around partial JSON fragments in streams, and make retries with idempotency and context cancellation easier for callers.
acceptance_criteria: Typed mapper helpers for text, chat, and structured JSON outputs (examples: TextResponse -> struct, ChatResponse -> []Message) implemented and unit-tested
Streaming transformer API that supports map/filter/split, preserves partial token fragments, and exposes a streaming-safe DecodeJSON helper
Retry helpers for streaming and non-streaming flows that support (a) idempotency keys, (b) graceful resume/fallback where underlying protocol allows, and (c) backoff hooks for caller instrumentation
At least three runnable examples in examples/streaming: structured-output decode, streaming retry on transient 5xx, and composing a streaming transformer pipeline
API surface reviewed by SDK/PM/Docs and backward-compatible with existing high-level client methods
Documentation page (Console/Docs) and GoDoc comments for all public helpers
A reviewable PR with CI green and integration test against the hosted sandbox model (runtime-qa)
implementation_plan: 1) RFC and design doc (drafted) -> discuss with SDK guild. 2) Implement core typed mappers (Text/Chat/Embedding wrappers) and small decoding helpers using generics to map bytes->struct. 3) Implement streaming transformer primitives: Transformer (func([]byte) ([]byte, error)), Splitter, JSONChunker that handles partial objects. 4) Implement retry wrapper that composes with transformers to allow safe retries when stream has not yet emitted user-visible output. 5) Add examples and integration tests; iterate on ergonomics based on internal usage. 6) Docs and release notes. Target: split work into two PRs: core mappers + non-streaming retries (PR-1) and streaming transformers + streaming retries + examples (PR-2).
tradeoffs: Expose too many small helpers => surface area and maintenance cost. We prioritize a small curated set (mapper, streaming.DecodeJSON, Transformer pipeline) over exhaustive utilities.
Providing automatic stream resume is desirable but risky across model variants; initial implementation will avoid automatic server-side resume and instead offer caller-facing resume hooks.
Generics-based mappers are type-safe but can be less discoverable for new Go users; provide clear examples and GoDoc to mitigate.
Performance: additional allocations in transformers could impact micro-latency; benchmark and optimize hot paths (reuse buffers, allow zero-copy where possible).
open_questions: Should the streaming retry helper buffer N tokens before deciding it’s safe to retry, or should we require caller-supplied idempotency for any retry?
Do we expose a high-level StreamingClient that owns transformers, or keep helpers as functions so users can compose with existing clients?
What is the canonical JSON-chunking behavior for nested structured output (multiple JSON objects vs newline-delimited JSON)? Agree on one approach for docs.
Edge-case: function/tool calling output that contains non-JSON chit-chat. How should DecodeJSON handle mixed content?
notes: 2025-03-10: Created RFC and spike prototype for JSON chunker (Lina). Spike shows partial-object buffering working with the streaming test harness.
2025-03-11: Prototype PR uploaded: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/542 (core mappers + tests). CI flaky on one test under race detector.
2025-03-12: Design review with SDK guild. Decision: prefer functional helper set over a big interface. Marco suggested a Transformer pipeline inspired by io.Pipe semantics.
2025-03-13: PM feedback (Aisha Patel): include a simple one-file example that engineers can paste into services to handle structured output from tools. Added to acceptance criteria.
2025-03-14: Added streaming-retry demo and updated docs draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/sdk-go-streaming-unmarshal (internal). Preparing PR-2 with transformer pipeline and examples.
qa_plan: Unit tests for every helper, fuzz tests for JSON chunker to ensure partial fragments do not yield invalid decode, integration test that connects to runtime-qa to validate streaming retry and non-streaming mappers, manual smoke test with sample service that uses the example to ensure ergonomics are straightforward.
docs_plan: Write a short 'Structured output in Go' docs guide with three runnable snippets: simple DecodeJSON example, streaming transformer pipeline example, and streaming retry pattern with idempotency keys. Add GoDoc comments and a changelog entry in release notes.
risks: API churn if early ergonomics are wrong; mitigate by keeping surface small and adding internal deprecated wrappers before breaking changes.
Performance regressions in hot paths if transformers allocate heavily; add benchmarks as gate for merge.
Complexity around resume semantics for streaming retries; initial release will document limitations clearly.
